name: B200

compute.precisionNote: Dense, no sparsity, derived from Nvidia's HGX B200 board table (8 GPUs: 36 PFLOPS FP16/BF16 and 72 PFLOPS FP8 with sparsity, 72 PFLOPS FP4 dense). name: H200 (China-licensed configuration)
status: Shipping in small volume to China

compute.precisionNote: Dense. Nvidia's H200 SXM page quotes 1,979 TFLOPS BF16 and 3,958 TFLOPS FP8 with sparsity; halved here. Hopper has no FP4 tensor core.

exportStatus: Licensable to China and Macau, case by case, since the BIS final rule effective 15 January 2026. That rule names the H200 and the AMD MI325X and sets the ceiling at total processing performance below 21,000 and total DRAM bandwidth below 6,500 GB/s; the H200's 4,800 GB/s and roughly 15,800 TPP fall under both. Aggregate TPP shipped to China is capped at 50 percent of aggregate TPP shipped to US customers, and a concurrent presidential proclamation adds a 25 percent tariff. Reexports and in-country transfers remain under presumption of denial. First deliveries to ByteDance and Tencent were reported in August 2026.
notes: Not a China-specific SKU but the standard Hopper part, readmitted through a licensing carve-out after the purpose-built B30A was blocked in November 2025 and the RTX Pro 6000D was rejected by Beijing in September 2025. It is the clearest case of export policy setting the product roadmap rather than the other way round.

memory.type: HBM (generation not stated) plus 384 MB on-die Vmem

process.node: 14 nm on the first-generation GroqChip; Groq says it is moving to a 4 nm class node
